summary: This informational document describes the URN namespace identifier for resources published by the Near Field Communication Forum, whose Technical Committee manages those resources.

eli5.summary: Names for things in the tap-to-pay style world needed a special prefix. This registers the prefix used by the group that runs that technology.

subtitle: Register the nfc URN namespace for the Near Field Communication Forum.

tldr.problem: The Near Field Communication Forum is developing specifications for near-field wireless communication but has no registered URN namespace for the resources it manages.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4729 registers the 'nfc' namespace identifier, allowing NFC Forum to create persistent, globally unique identifiers for their specifications, data types, schemas, and other resources.
tldr.outcome: NFC Forum resources can be unambiguously identified and managed across the internet.

today: RFC 4729 is an Informational RFC published in November 2006 and has not been obsoleted. The nfc URN namespace is registered with IANA and available for use by the NFC Forum and organizations working with near-field communication technologies.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Near Field Communication (NFC) Forum is an industry organization developing technologies and specifications for wireless communication between devices in close proximity. The NFC Forum's membership includes chip vendors, equipment makers, financial services, and other organizations building NFC capabilities into phones, payment terminals, and other devices.

As the NFC Forum develops specifications, they need to define and name resources such as data types, XML schemas, and protocol elements. To ensure these names are unique and persistent across time and organizations, the NFC Forum required a Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace. URN namespaces allow organizations to create machine-readable, non-location-dependent identifiers for resources they manage.
sections.eli5: NFC is the technology that lets your phone pay for things by tapping it on a terminal. The organization running NFC needed a special naming system for all the technical details they create.

sections.title: The nfc URN Namespace
sections.content:
RFC 4729 registers the nfc Namespace Identifier (NID). URNs using this namespace follow the structure urn:nfc:{NFCresource}:{ResourceSpecificString}. The NFCresource part identifies a class of resource (such as "wkt" for well-known types or "schema" for XML schemas), and the ResourceSpecificString provides the specific identifier within that class.

Examples include urn:nfc:wkt:Uri, which identifies a well-known type for URI bookmarks defined by NFC Forum, and urn:nfc:schema:manifest, which identifies an XML namespace for manifest elements. The NFC Forum's Technical Committee manages the assignment of resource classes and specific registration values.
sections.eli5: The naming system is urn:nfc:type:name. Like urn:nfc:wkt:Uri means a name bookmark type. The NFC Forum decides what types and names to create.

sections.title: Managing the Namespace
sections.content:
The NFC Forum commits to ensuring uniqueness of resource names assigned within the nfc namespace. The Technical Committee coordinates creation of new resource classes based on community need. For resource classes open to self-assignment, fully-qualified domain names are incorporated into the identifier to distinguish different naming authorities.

The RFC notes that while domain names provide some uniqueness, no absolute guarantee of long-term uniqueness can be made beyond the guarantee for domain names themselves due to domain transfers and abandonments. However, the NFC Forum promises not to reassign names, guaranteeing persistence of identifiers for the lifetime of the named resource and beyond.
sections.eli5: The NFC Forum promises to not reuse names once they are assigned. If someone gets a name, it's theirs forever. For self-assigned names, domain names are used to prevent conflicts.

sections.title: Registration and Resource Classes
sections.content:
The NFC Forum provides three types of registration activities. Registered names are associated with NFC Forum specifications or services. Delegated registration allows the Forum to register names or resource classes for external organizations, subject to requirements for maintaining uniqueness. Experimental names can be registered for testing purposes.

Resource classes are organized by type. The namespace is not associated with a Resolution Discovery System (RDS), meaning URN resolution for these names is handled outside the standard URN resolution infrastructure. The NFC Forum handles validation and assignment through procedures documented in their registration process specifications.
sections.eli5: The NFC Forum keeps a registry of resource classes and manages who gets what name. They have procedures for registering new ones, delegating to partners, and testing experimental names.

sections.title: Scope and Technical Considerations
sections.content:
The nfc namespace has global scope and can be used anywhere URNs are processed. The namespace maintains lexical equivalence rules consistent with RFC 2141 (URN syntax) and has no special validation requirements beyond standard URN syntax compliance. The namespace does not employ a resolution mechanism, so applications relying on these URNs must obtain resource definitions directly from the NFC Forum or through embedded knowledge.

The RFC emphasizes that many NFC Forum specifications and resources are made available to the broader community beyond the Forum's direct membership, supporting industry interoperability and adoption of NFC technology.
sections.eli5: These names can be used anywhere in the world. The URN syntax is standard. There's no automatic lookup system; you get the actual specification from the NFC Forum directly.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R., and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
